name: Kest with Chromium
author: kest@users.noreply.github.com
description: Kest is a personal accountability assistant that runs as a Telegram bot. It helps you stay consistent with workouts, meals, sleep and focus, and connects to services such as Gmail and Notion through plugins. Requires the custom browser image built from deploy/docker/Dockerfile.browser and host support for Chromium user namespaces.

installation.script:
#!/bin/ash
# Kest installation script for Pterodactyl.
#
# Runs inside ghcr.io/pterodactyl/installers:alpine with the server volume at
# /mnt/server. The panel passes egg variables as environment variables.
#
# This file is the source of truth. `go run ./scripts/sync-egg` copies it into
# deploy/pterodactyl/egg-kest.json.
#
# KEST_VERSION is a release tag such as v0.1.0-beta.1, or "latest": the newest
# stable release, or the newest pre-release while no stable release exists.

set -eu

REPO="Harfull/Kest"
VERSION="${KEST_VERSION:-latest}"

# tag_from prints the tag_name of the first release in a GitHub API response
# fetched from the given URL, or nothing if the request or parsing fails.
tag_from() {
  curl -fsSL -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' "$1" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -m1 '"tag_name"' \
    | sed 's/.*"tag_name"[^"]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/' || true
}

# resolve_tag prints the release tag to install.
#
# GitHub's "latest" endpoint ignores pre-releases, so while Kest is in beta it
# answers 404. In that case the newest release of any kind is used.
resolve_tag() {
  if [ "$VERSION" != "latest" ]; then
    echo "$VERSION"
    return 0
  fi
  tag="$(tag_from "https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases/latest")"
  if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
    tag="$(tag_from "https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases?per_page=1")"
  fi
  if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
    echo "kest-install: no releases found for ${REPO}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "$tag"
}

# Tests source this file for the functions above without running the install.
if [ "${KEST_INSTALL_LIB:-}" = "1" ]; then
  return 0
fi

cd /mnt/server
mkdir -p data

case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64 | amd64) ARCH="amd64" ;;
  aarch64 | arm64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
  *)
    echo "kest-install: unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

TAG="$(resolve_tag)"
case "$TAG" in
  *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]* | "")
    echo "kest-install: invalid release tag: ${TAG}" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

BASE="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${TAG}"
ASSET="kest-linux-${ARCH}"

echo "kest-install: downloading ${ASSET} (${TAG})"
curl -fsSL -o kest.download "${BASE}/${ASSET}"
curl -fsSL -o checksums.txt "${BASE}/checksums.txt"

expected="$(grep " ${ASSET}\$" checksums.txt | cut -d' ' -f1)"
actual="$(sha256sum kest.download | cut -d' ' -f1)"

if [ -z "$expected" ] || [ "$expected" != "$actual" ]; then
  echo "kest-install: checksum mismatch for ${ASSET}" >&2
  rm -f kest.download checksums.txt
  exit 1
fi

chmod +x kest.download
mv kest.download kest
rm -f checksums.txt

echo "kest-install: installed ${TAG}"

variables.name: Telegram Bot Token
variables.description: Token from @BotFather. Treat it like a password.

variables.name: OpenRouter API Key
variables.description: API key from openrouter.ai. Treat it like a password.

variables.name: Owner Telegram ID
variables.description: Numeric Telegram user ID(s) allowed to talk to Kest. Separate several with commas. Message @userinfobot to find yours.

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Your IANA timezone, for example Europe/London or America/New_York. Used for every schedule.

variables.name: Kest Version
variables.description: Release tag to install, for example v0.1.0-beta.1, or latest (the newest stable release, or the newest beta while no stable release exists). Takes effect on reinstall.

variables.name: General Model
variables.description: OpenRouter model for conversation and tool use. Must support tool calling.

variables.name: Fallback Models
variables.description: Optional comma-separated OpenRouter models to try if the general model fails.

variables.name: Transcription Model
variables.description: OpenRouter speech-to-text model for voice notes.

variables.name: Text-to-Speech Model
variables.description: OpenRouter text-to-speech model for voice replies.

variables.name: TTS Voice
variables.description: Voice name for the text-to-speech model. Voices differ per model; if the model rejects it, Kest tries a built-in voice for the model.

variables.name: Daily Budget (USD)
variables.description: Kest pauses proactive messages and costly calls once this much is spent in a day. 0 disables the limit.

variables.name: Max Proactive Messages Per Day
variables.description: Upper limit on messages Kest sends without being asked.

variables.name: Plugins
variables.description: Built-in plugins to load, comma separated. Available: reminders, tasks, webfetch, browser (requires the browser runtime image).

variables.name: Data Directory
variables.description: Where Kest keeps its database, config and backups. Leave as is.

variables.name: Chromium Sandbox
variables.description: Keep true. The Wings host must support Chromium user namespaces; no automatic fallback is allowed.

variables.name: Headless Browser
variables.description: Use false only with the desktop image and a private noVNC tunnel.
